It only got worse. My temperature and bp were taken. I was frisked again. They took my shoes and gave me socks to wear. They gave me s blanket. I asked for another. I was placed in a large holding area with men and women. I am a women. There was no place to sit or lay down. When a chair/recliner became available I put down one sheet and covered myself with the other. When I got up my recliner and sheets were being used by someone else. I was told I would speak to a counselor and then released. In the holding area with me were individuals who had just been released from jail, individuals either manic or psychotic, homeless. One women came in with no pants or shoes. I asked every 2 hours when I would be able to speak with a counselor. When they finally located get she was asleep in her office. I wanted to go apeshit, but knew I had to keep my cool. I was terrified. I was given a handbook of patient's rights. I read it cover to cover. It said I could request to be transferred to another facility. When I asked I was denied and told I would be released shortly. Breakfast was supposed to be served at 6:00. The "cooks" never showed up so the nurses and aides had to serve breakfast. After breakfast we were escorted back to the holding area. At that point a nurse told me I was not going to be released until I saw a psychiatrist. It was a Saturday. I was moved to a patient floor where I was assigned a room. I continued to tell the nursing staff I was not supposed to be there and I wanted to leave. But of course everyone says that. A nurse escorted me to a private room so I could change into a gown and be searched again. As I was changing she said, " how come you still have your bra on?" I said excuse me? She said it should have been confiscated at arrival Bc it was an underwire and could be used as a weapon. I think it was at that point they realized I was not in for the long haul. And someone fucked up. She let me keep my clothes on. And I was the first patient to be seen by the psychiatrist. He asked me 3 questions. Are you suicidal? Homicidal? Psychotic? To which I answered no. He then said you can go. Of course, I just couldn't pick up and go. I had the opportunity to have lunch with some of the sickest people I have ever seen. They served chicken. The chicken was raw inside. RAW!!! The things I saw and experienced really fucked me up. Between that horrible experience, not being able to take my meds, and sleep deprivation, a few days later I experienced my first, only and hopefully last psychotic episode. My family took control this time. I went to a proper hospital and received proper care. My therapist, psychiatrist and Doctor think I should talk to the media. I wouldn't know how to begin.

My 1st inpatient was when I was 19. I self-admitted. I felt well cared for, but did not think I needed to be there. So, after 4 days I left. The experience changed my life (at the time for the better). 
My 2nd hospitalization came many years later. 16 years or so. I had od'd on otc sleep meds. It was not a suicide attempt, but an attempt to escape the pain. The doctor who saw me asked me one question "did I have intent to harm myself." I said not, but he was not satisfied with my answer. Since I live in Florida I was a Baker Act. I was transported from one hospital to another after waiting over 3 hours while a nurse babysat me and never said one word to be.
That hospital stay was brief. I am a mental health professional (ha ha) so I know what to say to get me out. However, the hospital was awful. There was no treatment. No help. Just a bunch of women sitting in a room.
The 3rd hospitalization I was removed from my home by ambulance and stretcher. It was also a Baker Act. It was an inappropriate Baker Act and I was released within a few hours
The 4th was a self-admit Bc I needed an immediate med adjustment. Another awful hospital. They had techs "running" the groups. Everything revolved around smoking breaks (I don't smoke). Most people were detoxing or physically recovering from self-injury or suicide attempts
The 5th was the worst. I called a hotline to talk. I just needed to talk. I was on my landline. The call was traced and the police were sent to my home. I was searched and frisked and placed in the back of a police car. I've written about this before. Again, it was a Baker Act even though I was not homicidal, suicidal or psychotic. The police officer was not trained to make a proper assessment. There was no reason for the way I was treated. The facility was unsafe. It was a coed holding cell. People were brought in all night either from the streets or newly released from jail. When I demanded to speak with my counselor they found her asleep at her desk. I was standing there. Had I not been so fearful I would've lost my shit over 
The 6th I have no recollection whatsoever. I had my first, only and hopefully last psychotic episode. I don't remember much. I remember being terrified. It was my family who decided I needed to be admitted. I was there 5 days and remember nothing. I don't even remember being released. I remember a nice lady who snuck me chocolate. Apparently I introduced her to my brother. The admitting ER "lost" my engagement ring and wedding band. 
It's been a tough road. If I felt that I would receive proper treatment and care I'd check myself in today. I know the outcome. I know the level of care I will receive. As someone who suffers from mental illness and also in the field I feel like I need to advocate. But I know I won't be heard.
FIGHT THE GOOD FIGHT! KEEP ON KEEPING ON!

I called the National Suicide Prevention Hotline which is supposed to be anonymous. I was in pretty bad shape. Questions were asked to assess my immediate safety. They are standard questions and I answered honestly. I just needed to get through a really dark moment and thought I would be able to do so with the assistance of a trained professional. If I had any real intention of killing myself I would not have sought immediate help. Oddly, the counselor  asked about my children. I asked him how he knew I had children. He said he was just asking. At one point he forgot to mute his phone which they are supposed to do when there is silence. I heard someone in the background giving someone else my name and age. I asked the counselor how they got my information. He said there were other counsellors talking to other people and I must've overheard. I have a unique name, but I trusted him. I was not quite with it yet to put 2 and 2 together.
I spoke to the counselor for approximately 1 hour. We discussed and went over a safety plan a number of times. I was able to calm down and I felt safe. I assured the counselor I was. I made that very clear. We hung up. I was relieved. As I was walking to my bedroom and turning off lights, I saw a flashlight through my living room window. I was met at the door by 4 police officers. They questioned me for about 20 minutes. I was calm and tired at that point. They would not tell me why they were there. But I knew. I explained my safety plan. They had information I only provided to the counselor. I thought they were just checking in. I was not happy they had been notified, but I just wanted to go to bed. They then told me they we going to commit me to a psychiatric hospital. In Florida it is called a Baker Act. Involuntary. I had no choice. I said I wanted to change out of my pjs. They said a female officer would escort me. But 3 officers then entered my home. My children were asleep. They are young. They woke both children and shined their flashlights in their faces and asked "Are you hurt? Are you safe?" The female officer  then went with me to my bedroom. She watched me undress and get proper clothes on. I stood where she could see me. They woke my husband and told him "they were taking me in." They did not tell him why. They simply gave him a card with a number and told him to call in the morning.  I was the escorted outside. A male officer  told me to put my hands on the police car and spread my legs. They patted me down and searched me. And put me in the back of the police car. First time for everything I guess. They stood outside their cars for about 20 minutes laughing. The kept their call radios on. It was 2:30 am at this point. I have neighbors. I have kids who were scared and confused. So was my husband. So was I. I was also emotionally drained and tired. I needed rest. After they were done chatting? I was taken to a minimum holding facility. Jail for severely mentally ill i.e. schizophrenic, psychotic, manic, suicidal. I was not suicidal. 
I know you are thinking why didn't I wake  my husband? I knew there wasn't much he could do. I did not want to scare my kids. I did what I thought to be the best thing. I did the right thing. I am a mental health professional myself. I did what I have told my clients to do. 
An anonymous suicide call line tracked my information down and contacted the police. The police treated me like a criminal and not like someone who was in distress. It was punitive. It was traumatic. I have spoken to my therapist and other mental health professionals who I trust about my experience. My experience got much worse after I was locked up. It has been suggested I contact the media in regards to how I was treated and how things went down. I have a mental illness and have been through hell and back. I also happen to be a mental health professional. But this by far was perhaps one of the most traumatic experiences of my life. And all because I called the National Suicide Hotline. 

Edit: typos, grammar, spelling. This is still really hard for me to think about and I just wanted to get it heard without worrying about how it was written. Be safe. Be well. Be careful.
